nameTh: ฉะเชิงเทรา

town.name: Mueang Chachoengsao (Chachoengsao town, on the Bang Pakong River)

households.home: farmhouse on the western river plain
households.livelihood: rice farming on the low Bang Pakong plain

households.home: rented house in Phanom Sarakham district
households.livelihood: works in an electronic-waste recycling factory; 28 new recycling plants opened after the 2018 import ban, mostly in Ko Khanun subdistrict

landmarks.name: Wat Sothonwararam
landmarks.note: Riverside temple on the Bang Pakong, first named Wat Hong in the late Ayutthaya period; its main hall is on the provincial seal and shelters the Buddha image Luang Pho Sothon.

landmarks.name: Bang Pakong River
landmarks.note: The river running past the town and the rice plain.

landmarks.name: Khao Ang Rue Nai Wildlife Sanctuary
landmarks.note: Large forested hill sanctuary of about 1,078 sq km in Tha Takiap district.

households.livelihood: durian growing; in 2000 the province produced about 380,000 tonnes, around 45.6% of Thailand's durian
gem trade; Chanthaburi and neighbouring Trat are a centre of ruby and sapphire mining and trading
ethnic Vietnamese Catholic family, a significant minority who arrived in three waves; the town has been a bishop's seat since 1944

landmarks.name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
landmarks.note: Neo-Gothic cathedral with twin spires and a nave with two side aisles, visible from much of town; begun 1904, inaugurated 1909.

landmarks.name: Khao Khitchakut
landmarks.note: Mountain with a sacred balancing rock and a Buddha footprint on its summit.

landmarks.name: Phlio Waterfall
landmarks.note: Forest waterfall in Namtok Phlio National Park, which the provincial slogan celebrates.

town.name: Laem Chabang (port city, Si Racha and Bang Lamung districts)

households.home: rented room near the industrial parks
households.livelihood: factory work; over 200 companies operate in Laem Chabang, and the Saha Group park alone has about 80 factories with 20,000 employees
pineapple plantations, which have declined sharply as industry grew

households.home: rented room, registered at home in another province
households.livelihood: migrant worker; about 60,000 people work in Laem Chabang without registering residence there

landmarks.name: Laem Chabang container port
landmarks.note: Gantry cranes and container terminals along the shore; development began 1988, container port completed 1991.

landmarks.name: Sanctuary of Truth, Pattaya
landmarks.note: All-timber temple-castle of carved teak with a 105 m central spire; construction began 1981. 1981 is when construction began; it is still being built.

landmarks.name: Khao Khiao range
landmarks.note: Low mountain range running northwest to southeast across the province.

landmarks.name: Bang Saen beach
landmarks.note: Gulf beach, known for its Songkran sand-Buddha contest.

nameTh: ปราจีนบุรี

town.name: Si Maha Phot (Rojana Industrial Park area, Tambon Hua Wa)

households.home: rented room near the industrial park
households.livelihood: factory line work; manufacturing is about 71% of provincial output and 84.5% of workers are outside agriculture
technician or office staff at the Honda plant in Rojana Industrial Park (opened March 2016)

landmarks.name: Honda plant, Rojana Industrial Park
landmarks.note: Large car factory with an initial capacity of 60,000 vehicles a year; opened March 2016.

landmarks.name: Wat Si Maha Phot and its Bodhi tree
landmarks.note: Temple of the district's namesake Bodhi tree, said to have been planted about 2,000 years ago.

landmarks.name: Sa Morakot and Si Mahosot ancient town
landmarks.note: Moated ancient town with Buddha footprint carvings, an ancient reservoir and a Khmer-era hospital of the late 1100s.

landmarks.name: Khao Yai National Park
landmarks.note: Forested mountain park; highest peak Khao Rom at 1,351 m.

households.livelihood: works in the Map Ta Phut Industrial Estate (151 factories; petrochemicals, refining, power and steel)

households.home: village house inside the estate zone
households.livelihood: one of about 30 agricultural and residential communities (over 49,000 residents) living in the industrial zone

households.home: house in Na Dan village on Ko Samet
households.livelihood: tourism, the mainstay of the island's economy; many residents settled without formal land title

landmarks.name: Map Ta Phut Industrial Estate
landmarks.note: Gas-processing plants and flares at the largest industrial park in Thailand; opened 1990.

landmarks.name: Ko Samet
landmarks.note: Small forested island shaped like a letter t, with beaches on its east coast; on the provincial seal.

landmarks.name: Khao Chamao waterfall
landmarks.note: Waterfall in Khao Chamao-Khao Wong National Park.

note: New archetype: a railway and market town at the Cambodian border, trade and second-hand goods rather than factories or orchards.

households.livelihood: second-hand clothing trade, a significant share of the town's trade, with Cambodians crossing daily with pushcarts
runs one of about 1,380 stores, most selling goods from the Cambodian side

landmarks.name: Rong Kluea Market
landmarks.note: About 66 acres of sheds in 40 panels of shops next to the border arch; opened in its present form 15 June 1991.

landmarks.name: Prasat Sdok Kok Thom
landmarks.note: Khmer temple known for a stone inscription dated 1052.

landmarks.name: Pang Sida National Park
landmarks.note: Forested park of 844 sq km.

households.livelihood: rubber planting; Trat has the third-largest rubber area in Thailand, about 55,461 hectares in 2017

households.home: stilt house over the sea at Bang Bao on Ko Chang
households.livelihood: fishing, which sustains many Ko Chang villages (Ban Salak Phet is the largest and oldest)

landmarks.name: Ko Chang
landmarks.note: Mountainous island with rainforest, waterfalls and coral reefs; highest peak Khao Salak Phet at 744 m; part of Mu Ko Chang Marine National Park.

landmarks.name: Khlong Kaeo waterfall
landmarks.note: Seven-level waterfall in Bo Rai district, near the Cambodian border.

landmarks.name: Khao Salak Phet
landmarks.note: Highest peak on Ko Chang at 744 m.
